Glossary

The words everyone uses and nobody defines.

Every one of these gets said in a meeting as though the whole room knows it. Most of the room does not, and asking in month three is worse than asking now. Plain definitions, why each one costs money, and a short clause on what Ordence does with it — including where the answer is nothing.

Rates and thresholds are the ones we hold for FY 2024-25 and every Finance Act moves some of them. Section 194H fell from 5 percent to 2 percent on 1 October 2024, mid-year, which is exactly why a printed rate goes stale. Use this to understand the shape of a rule. Use your CA for the number on the day.

GST

The words that decide whether an invoice is usable, and whether credit you have already claimed survives an assessment.

TermWhat it isWhy it matters, and what Ordence does
GSTINThe 15-character registration number: state code, the PAN, an entity code, the letter Z, a checksum character.A wrong one blocks your buyer's credit, and nobody notices until their month-end. Ordence validates the checksum on entry.
HSN and SACHSN codes classify goods, SAC codes classify services. The code decides the rate.Wrong code, wrong rate, on every invoice until somebody notices. Ordence holds rates as dated periods per code, so a March invoice keeps March's rate.
Place of supplyThe state a supply is treated as made in. It decides which tax you charge, not how much.Get it wrong and the total is right to the paisa and the document is still unusable: the credit lands in the wrong state's pool, and recovering tax wrongly paid is a separate application under Section 77 that takes months. Ordence derives it and records the sub-section it came from.
Place of supply for immovable propertySection 12(3). For construction, an under-construction flat, a works contract, a lease or an architect's fee, it is where the property is.Not where the buyer lives or where their GSTIN sits. A Maharashtra developer selling a Pune flat to a Karnataka company charges CGST and SGST. Generic engines answer from the customer record and get this wrong every time. Ordence will not compute the tax without a property location.
CGST, SGST, IGST, UTGSTIntra-state splits into CGST for the centre and SGST for the state. Inter-state is one head, IGST. In a union territory without a legislature, UTGST replaces SGST.The split follows place of supply and is never chosen by the person typing. Ordence rounds per line and then totals, because back-solving legs from a rounded total is how a split stops adding up.
ITCInput tax credit. The GST you paid suppliers, set off against the GST you collected from customers.Working capital, not bookkeeping. It is claimable only to the extent it appears in GSTR-2B, and Section 16(4) sets a deadline after which it is gone. Ordence attaches that deadline to the credit itself, not to a reminder.
Blocked credit, Section 17(5)Things whose GST can never be reclaimed. Motor cars, food and beverages, club memberships, and goods or services used to construct immovable property on your own account.A wrong answer produces a right-looking return, and the bill arrives years later with 18 percent interest under Section 50. On one mid-size tower the blocked amount is measured in crores. Ordence decides line by line, names the clause, and shows blocked beside claimable rather than netting it away.
Reverse charge, RCMCases where the buyer pays the GST instead of the supplier collecting it. Legal services, goods transport, imported services.Easy to miss, because the supplier's bill shows no tax at all. Ordence carries the flag and prints the declaration the invoice rules require. Paying and claiming happens in the return your CA files.
GSTR-1The statement of what you sold in a period, filed monthly or quarterly.It is where your customers' credit comes from, so filing late means your buyer chases you. Ordence holds the invoice register behind it and files nothing.
GSTR-2BA static monthly statement the government builds from what your suppliers filed. It is the ceiling on the credit you may claim.An invoice your supplier never uploaded is not credit, it is a receivable from someone holding your money. Ordence imports the portal JSON or the Excel export, matches with confidence scores, and leads with credit at risk. It never logs into the portal for you.
GSTR-3BThe monthly summary return where the tax is paid. Table 4(A) is credit available, Table 4(B) is credit reversed.The two are reported separately, so netting them in your books leaves you unable to fill the form. Ordence summarises the ITC register in that shape.
E-invoice and IRNAbove a turnover threshold, business-to-business invoices must be registered on the Invoice Registration Portal before issue, returning a reference number and a signed QR code.Without the IRN it is not a valid tax invoice and your buyer's credit is at risk. Ordence does not do this — no portal connection, no IRN field. If you are inside the threshold, raise it in the first conversation.
E-way billAn electronic permit to move goods above a value threshold, generated on the NIC portal, with validity tied to distance.A vehicle stopped without one is a detention while the driver waits for somebody to find a number. Ordence records the number and date on the challan and generates nothing.

TDS and paying suppliers

Withholding tax is where a small error is silent, compounds, and arrives two years later as somebody else's problem that turns out to be yours.

TermWhat it isWhy it matters, and what Ordence does
TDSTax deducted at source. You withhold a slice of certain payments, deposit it against the payee's PAN, and pay them the rest.The liability is yours, not theirs. Miss it and Section 201(1) makes you an assessee in default for the whole amount, interest runs, and 30 percent of the expense is disallowed under Section 40(a)(ia). Ordence stores the rate and statutory reference on each row, so a rate change today restates nothing.
Section 194CContractors and sub-contractors. 1 percent to an individual or HUF, 2 percent to anyone else.The trap is the aggregate. Four payments of twenty-five thousand look safe one at a time and cross the annual limit together — and once crossed, tax is due on all of it. Ordence shows that catch-up separately, because an accountant who cannot see it cannot explain it to the contractor.
Section 194HCommission and brokerage. 2 percent, down from 5 percent on 1 October 2024.A mid-year change is how a business over-deducts in November and under-deducts in August of the same year. Channel-partner brokerage runs through this section, and Ordence deducts it from the same constants the partner statement uses.
Section 194IRent. 2 percent for plant and machinery, 10 percent for land, building or furniture.The payment most often forgotten, because rent goes out by standing instruction and never passes an approval screen.
Section 194JProfessional or technical fees. 10 percent professional, 2 percent technical.Two rates in one section, and the difference is not obvious — a consultant and a testing lab can bill the same amount and attract different tax. Ordence treats them as separate rules, not one average.
Section 194QPurchase of goods beyond 50 lakh from one seller in a year. 0.1 percent, and the only common section where tax is on the excess rather than the whole.Sixty lakh of cement from one supplier is 0.1 percent of ten lakh — a thousand rupees. The ordinary rule over-deducts sixfold and the supplier cannot get it back from you.
Section 206AANo PAN on file. The rate becomes 20 percent, or the section rate if higher.A vendor who has not given you a PAN is one you are about to under-deduct from. Ordence resolves 206AA, 206AB and any Section 197 certificate in one place and records which won.
Section 206ABA payee who has not filed their own returns. Twice the section rate or 5 percent, whichever is higher.Somebody else's compliance failure becoming your cost and your conversation. Ordence flags the vendor and doubles the rate.
Section 201(1A)Interest on tax deducted and not deposited. 1.5 percent per month, part of a month counted as a whole month.Depositing on the eighth instead of the seventh costs a full month. Ordence computes it in whole months, the reading a notice arrives with.
Form 16AThe quarterly certificate you give a vendor for non-salary deductions, downloaded from TRACES once the return is processed.Vendors chase it, because without it they cannot claim credit for tax you took from them. Ordence tracks which quarters are open. TRACES generates it.
MSME and Section 43B(h)A registered micro or small enterprise must be paid within 45 days where there is a written agreement, 15 days where there is not. Pay later and the expense is disallowed that year.Only micro and small are covered — medium enterprises are not, which is the detail most people have backwards. A real expense stops being deductible until the year the money moves. Ordence keeps MSME status on the vendor and the 45-day clock beside the ageing.

Operations

Less frightening than the tax words and responsible for more arguments, because two people can use the same term and mean different quantities.

TermWhat it isWhy it matters, and what Ordence does
Three-way matchThe control where the purchase order, the goods receipt and the supplier invoice must agree before payment is released.It stops you paying for a hundred bags when eighty arrived. Ordence records receipts as stock movements and reconciles an invoice against its own lines and tax. A formal three-way match with tolerances is not built — if that control is why you are buying, say so at scoping.
Ageing bucketOutstanding money grouped by lateness: 0 to 30 days, 31 to 60, 61 to 90, over 90.It is what a bank asks for before releasing a tranche and what a collections meeting runs on. Ordence buckets receivables and payables alike, with accrued interest beside the buckets rather than inside them.
Reorder levelThe quantity at which an item should be reordered, with a reorder quantity and a lead time in days beside it.Without the lead time the level is a guess dressed as a policy. Ordence leaves it empty for items nobody reorders, so a one-off purchase does not look like an emergency.
Available versus on handOn hand is what is in the godown. Available is on hand minus what is already promised to open orders.Four hundred bags with three hundred committed to Thursday means a hundred are sellable. A screen that leaves that subtraction to a tired person sells the same cement twice. Ordence emphasises available.
Batch and lotA batch or lot number identifies a production run. A serial number identifies exactly one physical thing.It decides how fast you can answer a recall, a warranty claim or an expiry question. Ordence stores both on stock movements, and the database refuses a serial number on a movement of more than one unit.

Real estate

The words a developer's sales team, accounts team and lender each use slightly differently, which is why one project has three occupancy numbers.

TermWhat it isWhy it matters, and what Ordence does
RERAThe Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016. Registration, seventy percent of collections into a designated account, quarterly disclosures, and a defined rate of interest for delay.Section 2(za) makes that interest symmetric: the rate you charge a late buyer is the rate you owe a buyer you delayed. Ordence compares your agreement rate against it and warns when they diverge, because only one survives a dispute. It connects to no portal and files nothing.
Carpet, built-up, super built-upCarpet is the net usable area within the walls, as RERA defines it. Built-up adds the walls. Saleable or super built-up adds a share of common areas through a loading factor the developer picks.Under RERA you sell on carpet. The other two are marketing numbers, and the loading factor is why two projects at the same rate per square foot are not the same price. Ordence stores carpet and built-up separately, so a rate is never quoted against whichever number was nearest.
AbsorptionBooked plus sold, as a proportion of the units that were actually on the market.The denominator is the whole argument. Thirty flats withheld for promoters were never on sale, and counting them as unsold makes a healthy project look like a failing one in a board pack. Ordence excludes blocked units from the denominator.
Channel partnerA broker or agency that brings buyers and is paid brokerage on a booking.The payout is commission, so Section 194H applies at 2 percent, and the partner notices if your statement disagrees with the tax you deducted. Ordence computes both from the same constants.
Occupancy certificateThe local authority's certificate that a completed building may be occupied.Without it buyers cannot register and lenders will not disburse. It also flips the GST answer: flats sold under agreements dated before completion are a taxable supply and construction credit is eligible. Sold after, the sale is outside GST and the credit is blocked. Ordence puts occupancy risk at the top of the land screen.
Construction-linked planA payment plan where each instalment falls due when a construction milestone is certified, rather than on a calendar date.It is the difference between collections that track the build and collections that outrun it. Ordence raises the demand when the milestone is certified, and recomputes delay interest from the original due date even after a cheque bounces.

The five where a wrong answer is invisible

Everything above can be got wrong. These five are the ones where nothing on your screen goes red, the return files cleanly, and the cost arrives years later.

  • Place of supply. The invoice total is correct and the document is unusable.
  • Section 17(5). A blocked credit claimed anyway produces a return that balances.
  • The Section 194C aggregate. Four correct-looking payments, four correct-looking vouchers, no error anywhere, and the contractor has already left the site.
  • The Section 16(4) clock. Credit you were entitled to simply expires, and the only symptom is a number that was never claimed.
  • Section 43B(h). The payment goes out on day sixty, the vendor is happy, and the expense quietly stops being deductible.

What this page is not

It is not advice, and Ordence is not your chartered accountant. Software can carry a rule, show its working and refuse to let a document out that contradicts itself. It cannot decide whether your tower is being built on your own account, whether a vendor is genuinely micro or small, or whether a pre-RERA agreement rate survives. Those are judgements, and they belong to a person who signs.

What we hold ourselves to is that every computed number can be traced back to the clause it came from, in a sentence somebody can check. A figure you cannot explain to your CA is a figure you should not file.

Questions people actually ask

Our CA handles all of this. Why does it need to be in the software?

Because your CA sees the data after it exists. If place of supply was chosen from the customer record in March, your CA is reconciling a wrong document in October. The point of the rules being in the system is that the document is right when it is issued, not corrected afterwards.

Are these rates current?

They are what we hold for FY 2024-25. The product itself stores the rate on each transaction rather than looking it up live, so a rate change never restates last year. Treat this page as the shape of the rule and your CA as the number.

You have said no to e-invoicing twice on this page.

Three times, and it is the most requested missing piece. It is the gap most likely to close first, and we will not put a logo on it before it exists.

Bring us the one you are least sure about.

Usually there is a specific rule that is costing you money or sleep — a blocked credit, a threshold, a demand nobody can explain. Tell us which, and we will tell you whether the product handles it or not.
